comments.content: In `stopRun`, `stopBusyRef.current` is reset to `false` in the `finally` block immediately after `await invoke("workflow_stop", ...)` resolves, but the 300ms reconciliation runs via `setTimeout` afterwards. During that 300ms window a fast double-click will re-enter `stopRun` (the guard is already released) and fire a second `workflow_stop` invoke before `running` is reconciled — the original "busy" intent only protects the in-flight call, not the post-stop reconciliation.

The 300ms re-check inside `stopRun` closes over `activeId` from the surrounding render. `activeId` is reassigned in several paths (`openWorkflow` line 144, `createBlank` line 172, save success line 481) — if the user switches the active workflow within those 300ms, the re-check will query the previous workflow's status and call `setRunning(false)`, which then disables the start button for the newly active workflow even though it may have never been running.
